input.question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?
input.ground_truth: The kidneys and eyes have a higher concentration of capillaries than other organs. High sugar levels in the blood cause capillary damage, thus the two are affected more. Here is an article from [_URL_3_](_URL_0_) and one from another [Reddit post](_URL_1_) in [r/diabetes](_URL_2_). Retino = eyes, Nephro = kidney, -pathy = denoting disorder in a part of the body. & #x200B; Hope that helps. & #x200B; R

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why DM type 2 affect kidneys and eyes more than other organs and cause diabetic retinopathy , nephropathy?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine your body is like a house, and the blood is like tiny pipes that bring food and water to every room (which are your organs).

Now, when someone has type 2 diabetes, it’s like there’s too much sugar in the blood, and the sugar is like too much candy in the pipes. Too much sugar can make the pipes get hurt over time.

The kidneys are like the water filters in the house, and the eyes are like the windows you look through. The sugar likes to stick to these places a lot. When too much sugar sticks to the filters (kidneys), they can get hurt and not work as well—that’s called nephropathy.

When too much sugar sticks to the windows (eyes), it can make it hard to see clearly—that’s called retinopathy.

Other parts of the house might get a little sugar, but the kidneys and eyes get more of it and get hurt faster. That’s why type 2 diabetes affects the kidneys and eyes more and can cause those problems.
